edits.statement: Let $t>1$ be a rational number. Is $\sum_{n\ge1}\frac{1}{t^n-1}=\sum_{n\ge1}\frac{\tau(n)}{t^n}$ irrational, where $\tau(n)$ counts the divisors of $n$? A conjecture of Chowla; Erdős (1948) proved it for every integer $t\ge2$.

edits.resultNote:
For rational bases $t=a/b>1$, $F(t)=\sum_{n\ge1}(t^n-1)^{-1}$ is irrational whenever $\log b/\log a<0.5728$, and a formalized refinement reaches $0.573290$. The previous thresholds were $1/2-1/\pi^2\approx0.3987$ (Bundschuh and Väänänen, 1994) and $0.405683$ (W. Cook, September 2026, self-published). Problem 1049 itself stays open: $t=3/2$, with $\log2/\log3\approx0.631$, is still outside the region.

Along the way, for every integer $q\ge2$ the numbers $1,F(q),F(q)^2$ are linearly independent over $\mathbb Q$, so the Erdős-Borwein constant $F(2)$ is not quadratic irrational. Both follow from one degree criterion for real algebraic bases: no relation of degree at most $e$ over $\mathbb Q(q)$ when $e\lambda\log M(q)<\log q$, with $\lambda=(42963+428220/\pi^2)/202140\approx0.42718$.

Thank you for this, and for sending it in so quickly after the OpenAI imaginary quadratic manuscript. It was read properly on 15 October, and this is a scope decision about how the site lists claims of this size, not a verdict on the mathematics.

The manuscript carries no author line, the repository belongs to a pseudonymous account, and there is no formalisation. Agreement between AI models does not count on the ladder. Your earlier entries were listed because Lean proofs stood behind them; a 15-page argument on deep external inputs cannot be checked that way here.

It was good to see the attribution revision after the comment in issue 1, and that comment is worth noting: it raised precedents, not a gap. The way back is open. edits.resultNote: Theorem 1.1 of arXiv:2610.13139: for every bounded nonempty simply connected planar domain $\Omega$, with no boundary regularity assumed, $|\Omega|\lambda_j(\Omega)>4\pi j$ for all $j\ge1$, equivalently $N_D(E)<|\Omega|E/(4\pi)$ for $E>0$ (eigenvalues counted with multiplicity, endpoint included). edits.statement:
How large can a family of distinct four-element sets be if no three of its members form a sunflower, that is, three distinct members whose pairwise intersections are all equal (an empty common intersection included)? Write $f(4,3)$ for this maximum.

Abbott, Hanson and Sauer (1972) gave $f(4,3)\le142$ and Abbott and Hanson (1974) gave $f(4,3)\ge54$. Axante, Budala, Chitic, Dumitru and Nacu (arXiv:2609.06175v1, September 2026, Table 1 and Theorem 6.9) improved the upper bound to 83, so $54\le f(4,3)\le83$. The exact value is open. The forcing-threshold convention used for Erdős Problem #20 is one larger than $f(4,3)$.

For an integer $k\ge3$, let $E_N^{k\text{-adic}}$ be the expected $N$th $k$-adic complexity of a uniformly random $k$-ary sequence of length $N\ge1$. Lin, Xiao and Chen derive a lower bound of the form $N/2-O(1)$ and ask, as Question 3.2: estimate an upper bound on $E_N^{k\text{-adic}}$.

The $N$th $k$-adic complexity of a sequence is the least $\log_k\max(|f|,|q|)$ over reduced rationals $f/q$ whose $k$-adic expansion begins with it (unrounded; the convention fixed in Section 1 of the manuscript, following Goresky and Klapper).

Declined, under "no stated open question", and on the ground your own submission sets out. Thank you for raising it so plainly.

edits.statement: Dow and Tkachuk asked (Question 4.8): assume that the closure of $A$ is pseudocomplete for every countable $A \subset C_p(X)$. Must the Tychonoff space $X$ be a $P$-space? decisions.message:
Thank you for this, and for a submission that is unusually candid about what it does and does not claim. Declined, and the reason is priority within the source you build on, not the mathematics.

What was checked on 15 October 2026: the Zenodo record opens and carries a clear AI contribution statement. The problem was read on erdosproblems.com/687, which asks for good estimates of $Y(x)$ and in particular whether $Y(x)=o(x^2)$ or even $Y(x)\ll x^{1+o(1)}$. The identity $Y(x)=j(P(x))-1$ is correct (it is the classical reformulation via the Chinese remainder theorem; it is how the erdosproblems page gets $Y(x)\ll x^2$ from Iwaniec), and a brute-force computation here confirmed it for the primes up to 2, 3, 5, 7 and 11 ($Y=1,3,5,9,13$). The deduction is sound.

The reason for declining: the OpenAI manuscript itself already contains this statement, unconditionally as far as that paper goes, dated 25 September 2026. Its Theorem 1.2 says that for every large $z$ and every choice of classes $a_p \pmod p$ for all primes $p\le z$, at least $cYV_0/B^2>0$ integers in $[1,Y]$ with $Y=\lfloor z^2/(\log z)^2\rfloor$ avoid every class. That is exactly $Y(z)<z^2/(\log z)^2$, the bound your note derives, and the paper's Section 3 introduces it as 'another form of the same covering problem'. Applying its Theorem 1.1 at the primorial gives slightly more, $Y(x)\ll x^2/(\log x\,\log\log x)^2$. So the answer to the first question of #687 belongs to that manuscript, and the catalog will credit it there rather than as a separate later entry.

Your submission did the useful thing of noticing the connection to #687 explicitly, which the OpenAI paper does not do by number. That connection is now noted on the Jacobsthal entry, crediting you. If you take this further, for example toward $Y(x)\ll x^{1+o(1)}$, the Maier-Pomerance range, or Erdos's weaker variant with $o(y/\log y)$ exceptions, that would be a new result and very welcome here.

edits.statement: Ghys conjectured in 1995 that every holomorphic Anosov diffeomorphism of a compact complex manifold is holomorphically conjugate to an automorphism of a complex infra-nilmanifold, and proved it for complex surfaces. Does the conjecture hold in complex codimension one, that is when $\dim_{\mathbb C} E^s = 1$ or $\dim_{\mathbb C} E^u = 1$? This case contains every compact complex threefold.
edits.posedBy: Étienne Ghys, Holomorphic Anosov systems, Invent. Math. 119 (1995), 585-614 (conjecture on p. 586)
edits.aiRole:
The paper's Declaration of AI Use says the author used an internal version of Intern-S2 (Shanghai AI Lab) through multiple rounds of dialogue to assist in developing the mathematical ideas and arguments. It does not say which lemmas or constructions came from the model. The author states that he independently verified all arguments and takes full responsibility.

Separately, Theorem A and Theorems 1.1 to 1.3, with the parts of Ghys's 1995 paper they rely on, were formalised in Lean by the Bin Dong and Ruochuan Liu team at Peking University with their formalisation agent SHEAF; Jiedong Jiang and Bin Wu did the formalisation and the human check of the final statements (paper v3, 13 October 2026).

With comments stripped, the library and Comparator/Solution.lean contain no sorry, admit, axiom declarations, opaque, unsafe, implemented_by, extern or native_decide; several comments still say 'Stage 2 sorry' and are stale. The four headline statements in Comparator/Challenge.lean were read: compact connected complex manifold, biholomorphic f, a smooth metric with an invariant continuous splitting and an iterate contracting each bundle, one bundle of complex rank one; conclusion a biholomorphism to $\mathbb C^d/\Lambda$ conjugating f to a hyperbolic complex-linear lattice automorphism. Theorems A, 1.1 and 1.3 take as a hypothesis HomotopyTorusRigidity (closed smooth homotopy n-tori, n at least 5, are homeomorphic to the torus), a 1969 theorem of Hsiang and Wall that is not in Mathlib; the definition read here is a true statement, so the hypothesis is not vacuous. The Comparator acceptance and the axiom list are the authors' own; there is no CI and nothing was run here. No independent formalisation anchors the statement (none found in Formal Conjectures), so Lean-checked, not Lean-verified.
edits.resultNote:
Jiesong Zhang proves that every codimension-one holomorphic Anosov diffeomorphism of a compact connected complex manifold is biholomorphically conjugate to a hyperbolic automorphism of a complex torus. This settles Ghys's conjecture in that case, and so for all compact complex threefolds, where Xu and Zhang (2024) recorded it as open.

The proof removes the topological transitivity assumption from Ghys's Theorem B to get a topological conjugacy to a hyperbolic toral automorphism, proves that both invariant distributions are holomorphic (the stable one by an $L^2$ estimate), and shows a torus with holomorphic invariant distributions carries the standard complex structure. Cantat (2004) had the codimension-one case for projective manifolds.

The paper also gives a nilmanifold example whose invariant distributions are smooth but not holomorphic, so the method stops at codimension one. The general conjecture remains open.
edits.significanceNote: Ghys's 1995 conjecture is the central rigidity question for holomorphic Anosov systems and is known across smooth dynamics; this entry is its codimension-one case, recorded as open even in dimension three in 2024. Level with the Hajlasz-Onninen maximal-function question at 24, above Szabo's equivariant Jiang-Su conjecture at 22, and well below the Anosov-Katok smooth realization entry at 42, a broader and older problem.

edits.name: The irrationality exponent of arctangents of positive rationals is 2
edits.statement: The irrationality exponent of an irrational $x$ is $\mu(x)=\sup\{\nu>0:0<|x-p/q|<q^{-\nu}$ for infinitely many coprime integers $p,q$, $q\ge2\}$; Dirichlet gives $\mu(x)\ge2$ and almost every real has $\mu=2$. Upper bounds have been obtained for values $\arctan(1/n)$: Tomashevskaya (2008) gave a general estimate, Salikhov and Bashmakova (2020) improved the bounds for $\arctan(1/3)$ and $\arctan(1/5)$, and Bai (2026) reported $\mu(\arctan(1/2))\le 8.585166\ldots$. Since $\arctan 1=\pi/4$, the case $r=1$ is the conjecture $\mu(\pi)=2$. Is $\mu(\arctan r)=2$ for every nonzero rational $r$?
edits.resultNote: Claimed: for every rational $r>0$, $\mu(\arctan r)=2$, and $\mu(\sqrt r\,\pi)=2$; negative $r$ follows since $\arctan$ is odd and $\mu(-x)=\mu(x)$, which is not formalised. Both are corollaries of a quadratic field criterion: if $D$ is a nonsquare integer, $x\ne0$ real, and $e^{2\sqrt D x}\in\mathbb Q(\sqrt D)$ has norm one, then $x$ is irrational and $\mu(x)=2$, with an ineffective threshold. For $D=-1$ and $x=\arctan r$, $e^{2ix}=(1+ir)/(1-ir)$. The case $r=1$ recovers the OpenAI release's $\mu(\pi)=2$, already a Candidate here; the method adapts that manuscript's determinant argument with the interpolation theorems of Liu, Jiang and Zhang (arXiv 2610.10192, $\mu(\log r)=2$).
edits.verificationNote: No independent mathematician has checked this yet. Negative $r$ is not formalised.
